correctness.rationale: PASS: Reconstructed the classification of nonletter Lyndon factors by exactly one, two or three 1s in w=0^a1 0^b1 0^c1 0^d. One-1 factors are 0^i1 (i>0); two-1 factors obey strict first run longer than middle; three-1 factors have initial run longer than both later runs, or the precisely resolved tie i=b>c. No duplicate two-one factors arise from the two adjacent pairs. The m=0 word 111 is handled separately. Summing positive parts and the indicator gives equation (1); rational gap summation gives the stated generating function. Case splits on the largest run prove the unique maximum 3m+2 and gap 3 at m>=4; Dirichlet lattice-simplex convergence and six explicit order-cone integrals give first and second limiting moments 19/24 and 37/45, hence 563/2880 variance, with O(1) and O(m) remainders from piecewise-linear Riemann sums. A wholly separate brute rotation checker tested 330 words m<=7 and independent aggregation through m=12, plus maxima m=4..12. These bounded tests corroborate, not prove, the universal statement.

originality.rationale: PASS qualified: Saari studies Lyndon source words and Fibonacci/Sturmian factors, whereas the claim counts factors in arbitrary non-Lyndon binary sources conditioned on three ones. Glen–Simpson–Smyth 2017 gives unconditional source-word expectation and unconstrained maxima, which cannot determine a conditional fixed-weight individual gap law, exact conditional aggregate, unique conditional extremizer, or its limit moments. No matching theorem was located through actual mathematical-index and bibliographic searches. The known general framework is credited, not claimed; unseen exact fixed-weight formulas remain a genuine priority risk.

Finite brute forcing is not a certificate for all m; universality relies on the run-gap proof and exact symbolic sums.

value.rationale: PASS: Distinct Lyndon factors are a standard factor-complexity invariant. Conditioning on exactly three markers gives a natural sparse-composition regime distinct from unrestricted random words. The full formula, rational census, sharp isolated extremum and nondegenerate variance law are structurally useful rather than an arbitrary finite computation.

final_claim: For linear ordered binary words of weight three, an exact formula in four zero-run gaps yields the rational aggregate Lyndon-factor series, a unique maximum 3m+2 and runner-up 3m-1 for m>=4, and a nondegenerate Dirichlet-simplex limit with mean 19/24 and variance 563/2880.
limitations: An unindexed exact three-marker factor formula or a refinement of the unconditional expectation may predate this result.
Finite brute forcing is not a certificate for all m; universality relies on the run-gap proof and exact symbolic sums.
Scientific validation is separate from administrative publication readiness; no GitHub edits or external certifications were performed.
